main_text.l: Circa A. C. 724. Hoc regnum di-cebatur initio Soprarba & Ripagorza: deinde capta Pampejopoli sive Pampelonâ dictum fuit regnum Pampelona; & tandem, quod nomen hodieq; obtinet, Navarra.
Aragonia primò fuit comita-tus; deinde A. C. 895. Sanctius Ka-so Arbaca regem sefe Aragoniæ appellavit.
Cæpit A. C. 1139. Primus Rex fuit Alphonsus.

page.notes: The page number is printed as "4o" with a small o; transcribed as 40. The left margin notes are set at the start of the canon paragraphs they stand beside. The right edge shows fragments of the facing page's text (for example "st", "m", "n", "d", "7", "I"); these are the neighbouring page and are not transcribed. The "Qvartum" initial Q is a large letter, joined to the word as Quartum. Some italic and roman distinction in "sive Pampelonâ" and "Aragoniæ" is uncertain from the scan.
